# Keysight Technologies (KEYS): conditional operating-value study

Research cutoff: October 19, 2026 UTC. Isolated staging package, not published. USD millions and million shares unless stated. Values per common share are USD. No current stock quote, current upside, return, recommendation or October price target is provided. Independent review required before release.

## Identity and eligibility

Keysight Technologies, Inc., CIK 1601046, NYSE ticker KEYS, US common stock. It is the first unfinished eligible US-listed row in the Atlas inventory after excluding already published issuers and foreign-only identifiers. No alternate share class or ADR conversion. Robinhood's [US KEYS page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/KEYS/) explicitly says users can buy or sell KEYS; this is public platform-support evidence, not verification of any particular user's account or jurisdiction. The FY2025 10-K identifies NYSE listing and legal issuer. No trading action was taken.

## Business and durable drivers

Keysight sells electronic design, emulation, validation, manufacturing-test instruments, software and services. Communications Solutions Group (CSG) covers commercial communications plus aerospace/defense/government; Electronic Industrial Solutions Group (EISG) includes semiconductor, general electronics and automotive/energy. It is an enabling supplier to AI network capacity, not an AI accelerator vendor or a pure AI revenue stream. Customer R&D spending, technology transitions, manufacturing capacity and defense programs all matter.

The July 2026 10-Q links commercial-communications demand to terabit solutions and 400G/800G/1.6T transceiver manufacturing capacity. These are management's explanations, not independently verified end-demand forecasts. The same filing shows 9M CSG revenue $3,700M versus $2,736M and EISG $1,463M versus $1,220M. TTM segment bridge: CSG 3,726 + 3,700 − 2,736 = 4,690; EISG 1,649 + 1,463 − 1,220 = 1,892; total 6,582. Acquisition contributions and favorable product mix make extrapolation risky. The forecast separately fades CSG and EISG growth rather than extending the latest quarterly growth rate indefinitely.

Sources: [FY2025 audited 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104625000127/keys-20251031.htm), [July 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104626000036/keys-20260731.htm), especially business discussion, segment tables and MD&A. Frozen local copies and field-level accession provenance accompany this study.

## Ten-year record, with actual comparability breaks

`history-v1.csv/json` contains FY2016–FY2025 annual revenue, operating earnings, cash flow, gross capex, depreciation, amortization, SBC, R&D, acquisitions, buybacks and balance-sheet fields. Each original source fact has tag, period, filing date, accession and units in `history-field-provenance-v1.json`. Original USD and share facts are scaled by 1 million; percentages remain fractions. Source selection uses the latest filed annual-duration observation through the cutoff, not an unqualified scrape of the first tag. Annual fiscal ends are October 31. These are ten reported observations, not a fully constant-perimeter organic series.

- Revenue progressed from $2,918M in FY2016 to $5,375M in FY2025, with FY2024 down to $4,979M from $5,464M. The 2017 Ixia acquisition changes the business perimeter. It is misleading to call the entire growth record organic.
- FY2017 and FY2018 operating income in later filings is $148M and negative $394M, rather than original $239M and negative $346M: pension non-service components were moved out of operating income. Use recast figures, and do not imply FY2016 has been retrospectively homogenized.
- ASC606 began November 1, 2018 under the modified retrospective method. FY2016–18 revenue remains under earlier guidance. No estimated restatement has been invented. FY2019 onward is the stronger accounting-comparability window.
- FY2018 includes a $709M goodwill impairment and substantial tax effects. Net income or GAAP operating margins in that year are not a steady-state profitability proxy. Later margins also include acquisition amortization, integration spending and SBC.
- FY2023 operating margin was 24.85%; FY2024 16.73%; FY2025 16.30%. R&D increased from $882M to $919M to $1,007M while revenue contracted and recovered, illustrating deliberate fixed-cost investment and operating leverage.
- FY2025 audited net income is $850M and diluted EPS $4.91, versus preliminary earnings-release $846M/$4.89. Both the preliminary detailed revenue table and audited table report $5,375M; the rounded $5.37B release headline is not a revenue revision. The study uses audited history; guidance scorecards retain release-time actuals and flag the difference rather than silently mixing vintages.
- CFO less gross capex is $1,281M in FY2025, $898M in FY2024 and $1,211M in FY2023. It is a descriptive levered cash-flow measure, not unlevered owner cash: CFO includes taxes, interest, working-capital movements and SBC addback. Company-reported free cash flow additionally counts government incentives, so it is not identical to this series.
- Cash-flow amortization is used separately from depreciation; it is not automatically capex maintenance. Acquisition cash payments can be recast in later comparatives; field-level accession dates make this visible. FY2018 latest comparative acquisition cash is $5M versus $11M originally.
- Exact year-end point-in-time common shares are not supplied by the selected standard tag. Those fields remain null, not substituted with weighted diluted EPS shares. Older debt-current and operating-lease tags may likewise be null; pre-lease-adoption zeros are not proof of no lease commitments. Latest point-in-time shares are taken directly from the quarterly cover.

Comparability source: [FY2019 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104619000110/keys-10312019x10k.htm), Notes 1–2 and comparative statements; [original FY2018 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104618000030/keys-10312018x10k.htm). This package preserves both originals and later comparatives.

## Capital needs, acquisition discipline and obligations

Physical capex alone understates investment. Instrument/software development requires R&D; acquisitions require purchase consideration and recurring integration. R&D is already an expense in the model's economic EBIT and is not charged twice. The model retains SBC as a cash-replacement expense and adds back only estimated physical depreciation through net capex; acquired-intangible amortization is not separately added back. Future economic margins must therefore be interpreted under this conservative convention, rather than pasted from non-GAAP segment margins.

Spirent was acquired October 15, 2025; portions were divested to Viavi. The audited acquisition consideration was $1,564M and divestiture proceeds $399M. Other 2025 deals include the Synopsys Optical Solutions Group and PowerArtist businesses. These purchases expand testing/design capabilities but introduce integration, intangible-asset valuation and capital-allocation risks. Latest 9M FY2026 Spirent acquisition/integration costs total $75M. A generic 1% of forecast revenue reinvestment allowance is an analyst estimate for continuing acquisition/intangible renewal, not an announced transaction or prediction of deal size. No unannounced large acquisition is assumed funded.

The July 31, 2026 bridge uses unrestricted cash $2,605M, excludes $17M restricted cash and excludes $188M long-term investments. Debt is deducted at $2,550M face rather than $2,517M carrying value. It separately reserves $76M retirement/post-retirement liabilities and $20M for the fixed-to-floating swap liability. This avoids treating the accounting debt discount/swap mark as free equity value. Operating leases stay in operating costs and are not deducted again as financing debt. These conservative reserves are simplifications, not actuarial or derivative fair-value appraisals.

The model deducts an estimated 8% of TTM revenue ($526.56M) as operating cash, then reinvests changes in that cash requirement. Exact 170,244,745 outstanding common shares are dated August 27, 2026, **27 days after** the July balance-sheet anchor. This date mismatch is explicit; no exact July or October count is claimed. Weighted diluted 173M is not treated as a point-in-time share count. Existing unvested awards are not valued grant by grant; a 3% extra-share diagnostic supplements the cash-replacement compensation convention.

Debt liquidity schedule: $700M April 2027, $500M October 2029, $750M July 2030 and $600M October 2034. The forecast repays those principal amounts in the corresponding rolling twelve-month periods. Debt principal affects the liquidity path, not operating FCFF, and is not double-subtracted from enterprise value. Coupon interest is conservatively charged for a full maturity year. The $600M fixed-to-floating swap makes its fixed 4.95% modeled coupon an approximation; a +200bp coupon liquidity shock is included in the sensitivity file. It changes debt-service liquidity rather than unlevered enterprise value; WACC uncertainty is tested separately. A $750M undrawn revolver is a maximum emergency-debt assumption subject to covenants and maturity, not guaranteed funding. The illustrative funding module does not model the revolver's April2031 expiry/refinancing or repayment of emergency borrowing; it is a funding-need detector, not a fully financed equity valuation. Any scenario requiring external funds suppresses its headline per-share value. Grant dilution, future funding structure, refinancing, tax attributes and liquidity timing remain incomplete in such a scenario.

## DCF specification and estimated paths

Anchor: July 31, 2026; evidence cutoff October 19. Forecast periods are rolling annual periods ending July 2027–July 2036, **not fiscal-year forecasts**. Therefore the next-period revenue is not to be directly scored against management's October FY2026 outlook. This is an updated-information conditional value at a dated anchor, not an executable current target or historical backtest.

`make_model.py` records inputs; `replay_dcf.py` computes all annual rows. For every year:

1. Grow CSG and EISG revenue separately; apply explicit economic EBIT margin.
2. Cash taxes = max(EBIT,0) × estimated tax rate; no loss tax shield is fabricated.
3. FCFF = NOPAT − (gross capex − depreciation + acquisition/intangible reinvestment + change in working capital + change in required operating cash + sustainable-capital top-up).
4. Check cash after operating flow, interest and scheduled principal. Use capped emergency debt then illustrative equity with issuance fees if needed; record new shares. Funded outputs are diagnostics only.
5. Terminal reinvestment is the greater of NOPAT × g / ROIC and the actual maintenance/acquisition/NWC/operating-cash floor. WACC and terminal ROIC must both exceed g. Growth converges to g in both segments. Positive terminal earnings and positive terminal distributable FCFF are mandatory.

All forward inputs below are **analyst estimates**, not management promises or consensus. Central economics: 22% cash tax, gross capex 3.5% of revenue, physical depreciation 2%, acquisition/intangible renewal 1%, marginal NWC 18%, operating cash 8%. Net physical investment is thus 1.5% before renewal and working capital. Terminal investment is never cut below these operating needs.

- Bear: CSG falls 12% then 4%, EISG falls 10% then 2%, followed by recovery and fade to 2%; economic margin begins 16%, troughs 15%, settles 20%; WACC12%, g2%, terminal ROIC12%.
- Base: CSG grows 18%,12%,10% before fading to3%; EISG grows8%,7%,6% before fading to3%; margin25% rising to27%; WACC10%, g3%, terminal ROIC18%.
- Bull: CSG grows25%,18%,15% before fading to3.5%; EISG12%,10%,8.5% before fading to3.5%; margin27% rising to30%; WACC8.5%, g3.5%, terminal ROIC22%.

TTM GAAP EBIT is $1,333M (876 + 1,116 − 659), or20.25% of $6,582M revenue. Q3 FY2026 GAAP EBIT is $461M/$1,846M, or24.97%. Thus the base starts near the latest quarter's GAAP margin but materially above TTM; its27% endpoint requires durable mix/integration gains. The30% bull margin is particularly demanding under the retained-SBC/no-amortization-addback convention and exceeds the recent reported GAAP record. It must not be confused with management's higher adjusted segment margins.

These paths span a downturn, sustained expansion, and unusually favorable network/test operating leverage. There is no probabilistic calibration or scenario weighting. Recent growth can exceed the base start rate, but the base assumes normalization as acquisitions annualize and customer budgets cycle. Margin uncertainty is particularly important because the model does not separately capitalize R&D or add back acquired-intangible amortization.

## Conditional results and what would change them

Model replay gives approximately $37.33 bear / $129.14 base / $251.28 bull per common share at the **dated July anchor with the disclosed August share denominator**. Corresponding enterprise values are $6.92B/$22.55B/$43.35B. Terminal value contributes about42%/55%/67% of enterprise value. All three specified cases clear the annual liquidity floor without new external funding. These numbers illustrate assumptions, not market mispricing. No current-price comparison is valid from this bridge.

`forecast-v1.csv` exposes 30 annual case rows. `sensitivities-v1.json` includes a20-cell WACC/g grid, economic-margin shocks, additional-share diagnostic and severe early-loss debt/equity funding stresses. The latter confirm that funding-dependent headlines are withheld. Sensitivity values remain model outputs; different WACC/g changes cannot fix stale capital facts or incomplete award claims.

Monitor order conversion versus capacity-driven demand, CSG organic growth after acquisitions annualize, China/export-control and tariff restrictions, R&D intensity, integration costs, deferred revenue and working capital, share count versus SBC, and cash used for acquisitions/buybacks. Latest 9M FY2026 income-tax provision is $66M, while cash income tax paid net is $127M; these are different measures. Both are below the model's normalized22% cash-tax assumption applied to positive operating earnings. It does not extrapolate tax refunds, investment gains or temporary tariffs into perpetuity.

## Management evidence and research limits

The eleven consecutive quarters Q1 FY2024–Q3 FY2026 exceeded the prior-quarter original revenue and non-GAAP EPS upper guidance bounds. This is a bounded release-to-release sample, not a search of every intra-quarter revision. Quality checks matter: Q3 FY2024 EPS excluding a $0.16 tax benefit was $1.41 versus $1.36 upper guidance; Q2 FY2026 EPS excluding tariff/refund effects was $2.58 versus $2.33 upper guidance, rather than reported $2.87. Q2 FY2026 revenue excluding one-time effects was $1,758M versus $1,710M upper guidance, compared with reported $1,717M. These issuer adjustments do not equal independently normalized earnings. The FY2026 outlook changed scope from initial ex-acquisition growth of at least7% to total growth just above20%, then high20s%, then32%; these are not four apples-to-apples forecasts. See the archived prepared remarks and individual release URLs in the appendix.

Management's record must be separated into forecasting precision, organic execution and acquisition capital allocation. The consecutive-quarter guidance appendix in `guidance/` compares original ranges with release-time outcomes, including adjustments that make an apparent EPS beat less informative. Prepared remarks are issuer management statements, not independent interviews. The study does not claim a complete interview archive or independently verified management credibility score. Strong short-term guide beats are not proof of long-run investment returns; the Ixia impairment and later acquisition spending are counterweights.

The file set is offline-replayable. Source originals are frozen; scripts write derived outputs only. Independent review must assess accounting comparability, capital bridge, dated-share treatment, funding suppression, terminal floors, assumptions and management evidence before any canonical integration. No existing company, original base case or Site was edited.
